results.title: Yoshua Bengio - Wikipedia
results.content: **Yoshua Bengio** OC OQ OBE FRS FRSC (born March 5, 1964) is a Canadian computer scientist, and a pioneer of artificial neural networks and deep learning. Bengio received the 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award, often referred to as the "Nobel Prize of Computing", together with Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun, for their foundational work on deep learning. Bengio, Hinton, and LeCun are sometimes referred to as the "Godfathers of AI". In November 2025, Bengio became the first AI researcher with more than a million Google Scholar citations. Bengio is the brother of Samy Bengio, also an influential computer scientist working with neural networks, who is senior director of AI and ML research at Apple. In March 2023, following concerns raised by AI experts about the existential risk from artificial general intelligence, Bengio signed an open letter from the Future of Life Institute calling for "all AI labs to immediately pause for at least 6 months the training of AI systems more powerful than GPT-4".
